messages.text: My miner needs repair.

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Happy to help get this sorted.

To start: which model is it, and what exactly is it doing (or not doing)?
It's a NerdOctaxe from order Order Shop····. The fan on the far left continues to work itself off the board and causes errors. Is there a way I can send you the miner and you repair it?
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill

Thanks, that helps. The NerdOctaxe fan is a mailed part in most cases, so let me pin down which failure this is before anything goes anywhere.

Two things:

1. When you say the fan "works itself off the board": is the fan physically coming loose from its mounting (screws backing out, fan sitting on the heatsink), or is the 4 pin connector working its way out of the fan header on the PCB?
2. What exactly does the error say on the screen or in the web UI (for example a fan speed / RPM warning, or an overheat shutdown)? The exact wording matters.

A clear photo of the fan and its header, plus a photo of the error on screen, would let me settle this in one go.
The small 2 inch fan sitting on the heatsink will come loose and then the miner stops mining. And if I don't catch it I get the error "Voltage Protection Guru Meditation #····
Let me look that exact error up rather than guess at it. One moment.
Searched the web · NerdOctaxe "Guru Meditation" voltage protection error
Searched the web · ESP-Miner "Voltage Protection" "Guru Meditation" NerdQaxe
Used rma verdict
Handed to the team · Part needed (fan + mounting hardware) and the exact Guru Meditation code #····

Good news: that is not a board problem. From what you describe, the board hashes fine as long as the fan stays put, and the error is the firmware protecting itself once airflow is lost. So this is a mounting and fan issue, not a dead miner.

On the error itself, I want to be straight with you: I checked the NerdQaxe/NerdOctaxe firmware issue tracker and I could not find a documented decode for Guru Meditation #···· specifically. I will not guess at it. I have passed it to JD, our hardware lead, along with the fan problem.

Two things that would help:

1. The firmware version shown in the web UI (Settings, or the top of the main page), so JD can decode that code against the right build.
2. A photo of the fan sitting on the heatsink, close enough to show how it is held down (screws, clips, or the long screws that pass through the heatsink fins).

In the meantime, power the unit off before touching it, and check whether the fan screws are present and biting. On these the fan should be pulled down firmly onto the heatsink, not just resting on it. If the holes are stripped or a screw is missing, say so and that tells us exactly which part you need.

The team has this and will confirm by email, usually within one business day. If you want a faster second pair of eyes, the Discord is very active: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate (JD).
I spoke with your support last week about this issue. Maybe your chat logs will explain.

I cannot see past chat transcripts, so I have nothing from last week on my side. The team can pull those up, and I have already put this case in front of them with everything you have told me today, so whatever was said before will line up with it.

What I still need from you is the same two things, and they are the fastest way to close this out:

1. The firmware version shown in the miner's web UI.
2. A photo of the fan on the heatsink, close enough to show how it is held down.

If you would rather not repeat yourself, just say so and I will leave it with the team to pick up the earlier thread.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that is a useful shot. What I can see: the board side on, three black blocks in a row (the heatsinks with the fan sitting against them), the small blue and clear module up top with its ribbon cable, a component with black heatshrink marked "TUBE 125C", a green connector low down, and the yellow XT60 power connector at the bottom left. The bottom black block clearly sits proud of the other two, pushed out past their faces, and I cannot see a single screw or clip holding any of them down in this view.

That matches what you described: nothing is actually fastening that fan, so it walks off under its own vibration.

One question to settle which part you need:

Can you tell me whether the fan is held by long screws passing through the heatsink into the board standoffs, or whether the black block the fan sits in is a 3D printed bracket? If you can see screw heads from the other side, a photo of that face would answer it.

If the holes are stripped or a bracket is cracked, that is the part to replace, and the board itself is fine. Your case is already with JD with the photo context, and the Discord is the quick route if you want hands on it sooner: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.

The miner is not running, so I do not have access to the firmware version.
It is unclear how the fan is attached. 
There are no obvious screws.
Searched the web · NerdOctaxe fan mounting screws heatsink 40mm assembly

Two things, and let me take the more important one first.

1. You said the miner is not running. I need to know what that means right now: with the power plugged in, does anything light up at all (screen, any LED on the board)? Or is it completely dead? That changes what we chase next.

2. On the fan: 
the NerdOctaxe uses dual Thermalright heatsinks
, and on those the small fan is normally held on by two wire retention clips that hook into the fin stack, not by screws. That fits exactly what you are seeing, no obvious screws and a fan that walks off. If a clip is missing, bent or never hooked, the fan has nothing holding it.

Can you take one photo looking straight down on that fan from above, so I can see whether the wire clips are there and hooked into the fins? That plus the power answer should settle it.

The miner is unplugged to prevent any electrical damage. 
There are no obvious "clips" holding the fans to the heatsink.

Good, that is the right call, and it also tells me something useful: the board is not dead, you shut it down deliberately. So we are still only dealing with how that fan is held on.

If there are no screws and no clips, then whatever was holding it is either missing or was never fitted. One step to confirm which:

Lift the loose fan off the heatsink (it should come away with no force, the unit is unplugged) and take two photos:

1. The underside of the fan, the face that sat against the heatsink.
2. The face of the heatsink where the fan was sitting.

What I am looking for is whether there are threaded holes or clip slots in the fins, or adhesive residue or a strip of double sided thermal tape. That tells us exactly which retention part is missing, and that is the part that needs to come to you.

Do not plug the unit back in while the fan is off the heatsink. Those chips will overheat in well under a minute without airflow.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That photo tells me what I needed. Here is what I can see:

- A small 40mm fan, label FQJD, model HDB4020VB, DC 12V 0.6A, with a four wire lead (blue, yellow, red, black).
- It is sitting in a black 3D printed bracket with two upright posts, and that whole bracket straddles the small finned heatsink on the voltage regulator area, just behind the big main fans.
- There are no screws and no clips on it. The bracket is a friction fit, it just sits over the heatsink.
- Top of the board: the yellow XT60 12V input, the green 30A blade fuse F1, nothing burnt or discoloured anywhere I can see.

So the picture is consistent end to end. That little fan cools the voltage regulators. When the bracket walks off, the VRs lose their airflow, and the firmware trips exactly the kind of voltage protection fault you quoted. The miner is protecting itself, which is why nothing is damaged.

The fix is to stop the bracket moving. Do you have a couple of small zip ····? One or two passed through the bracket and around the base of that heatsink will hold it dead still, and it is fully reversible. If you would rather not, say so and I will leave the proper retention part to JD.

Once it is held, plug in and tell me the firmware version from the web UI, plus the VR temperature it shows at idle. That is the last thing I want to confirm before I call this closed.
There are no clips. It looks as though the fan was pushed onto the heatsink.

That confirms it. The bracket is a push fit over the heatsink fins, nothing more. Nothing is broken, the grip has just gone slack, so vibration walks it off and the VRs lose their airflow.

So, one question: do you have a couple of small zip ····hand?

If yes: push the bracket back down fully onto the heatsink so it is seated square, then run one zip ····through the bracket and around the base of the heatsink, snug but not crushing anything, and trim the tail so it cannot touch a fan blade. Then plug in and tell me the firmware version and the VR temperature at idle from the web UI.

If no: do not run it loose, leave it unplugged. I will leave the proper retention part with JD, who has your case and the photos.
There is not enough space between the heatsink and the board to run a zip ····.

Good photo, that answers it. What I see edge on: the finned VR heatsink sitting flush against the board with no gap underneath, the big main heatsink below it with its wire retention bow across the fins, the small 4020 fan in its printed bracket at the right (I can see a screw head on the bracket), the XT60 and the green fuse up top, and the white nylon standoffs holding the board. You are right, there is no room to pass anything between that heatsink and the PCB.

Different route, no clearance needed: thread the zip ····between two of the heatsink's fins instead of under it. A thin tie slides down a fin gap, comes out the other side, and loops around the bracket. That clamps the bracket to the fin stack without going anywhere near the board.

Two things before you try it:

1. Use a thin tie, 2.5mm or less, and keep it away from the fan blades and the wiring.
2. Snug only. Do not crank it, the printed bracket will crack.

If the fin gaps are too tight for that, say so and I will stop improvising. In that case the right answer is a proper retention part, and JD already has your case and these photos.

I prefer to not attempt to jerry rig/improvise anything if there's a fix for this. 
Also, this is the way I received the miner. This is not modified from the kits I was sent.

That is completely fair, and it is the right instinct. I will stop suggesting workarounds.

To be clear on where this lands: nothing on your board is faulty. The V. fan bracket is a push fit with no retention, and as you say that is how it left us, so the fix is the correct mounting part, not anything you should be bodging at your end.

What I have done: my findings are with JD, our hardware lead, including the model, the fan (FQJD HDB4020VB 12V 0.6A), the push fit bracket with no clips or screws, the voltage protection trip when the fan walks off, and your photos. JD decides what part goes out and the team will confirm by email, usually within one business day.

Until then leave it unplugged. Without that VR fan held in place it will just trip again, and there is no point risking heat on the regulators.

If you want it moved along faster, the Discord is where JD is most responsive: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.

I will leave the miner unplugged, and will wait to be contacted.
Thank you for your assistance.

You are welcome. That is the right plan: leave it unplugged and the team will come back to you by email.

Thanks for the photos and for being patient with the questions, they are what made this quick to pin down. If anything changes in the meantime, or you want a second pair of eyes sooner, the Discord is there: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.
